drift_findings.rationale: Two approved upstream claims no longer describe the delivered system. (1) design.md Section 5.7 states the optional restart_history field is the sole focused durable extension; the change set ships a second durable extension — baseline_adoptions with the new adopted_absences list and the baseline-adoption gate kind including adopt-committed-deletions (src/contracts/durable-state.ts:197,472; src/contracts/schemas/v1/task-state.schema.json:760; src/contracts/gates.ts:76,276; src/contracts/durable-gate.ts:237) — absorbed from origin/main by user direction and now part of this phase's reviewed bytes. (2) design.md Section 10's Phase 4 scope covers status-skill migration, upgrade/constitution adapters, low-level retirement, contract-test inversion, docs, and host proof; the delivered phase additionally changes durable reconciliation semantics (absence-aware projection union, unrestorable and committed_absent classification, produce re-entry vs human deletion gate routing) and adds produce-time planned-final-phase re-derivation with two new fail-closed produce guards. Both deviations are recorded and re-reviewed only in phases/4/design.md Section 1.3; the parent design.md is not among this change set's outputs, so the approved architecture remains stale on durable state, gate vocabulary, and phase scope. Everything else — the two-tool advertised catalogue, migration-audit arm, local adopt adapter, read-only status skill, retirement of the low-level surface, and host proof — matches the approved upstream.

rule_findings.rationale: The phase design was updated and re-entered its review boundary for every deviation (Section 1.3; impl-notes records a fresh significant-revision review and approval before the milestone), which covers the phase-level governing document. The parent architecture was not kept truthful: upstream design Section 5.7 still asserts "The optional restart_history audit field is the sole focused durable extension", while the delivered change set carries a second durable extension — TaskStateV1.baseline_adoptions with the new adopted_absences list (src/contracts/durable-state.ts:197,472; src/contracts/schemas/v1/task-state.schema.json:760) and the baseline-adoption gate kind with its adopt-committed-deletions decision (src/contracts/gates.ts:76,276; src/contracts/durable-gate.ts:237). The change set modifies only phases/4/design.md and phases/4/impl-notes.md among governing documents; .archflow/tasks/api-refactor/design.md is not among the outputs, so the approved architecture remains inaccurate about durable state and gate vocabulary that this change ships.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: phases/4/design.md Section 1.3 records six human-directed mid-phase amendments (main merge absorbing baseline-adoption machinery, dev-mode launcher replacing self-cutover installs, unrestorable-projection recovery, host-proof rebinding, planned-final-phase re-derivation, committed-deletion adoption); impl-notes.md records the same plus a stale-projection-union fix and a legacy decisions-tuple archive twin.

rule_findings.rationale: Every new advancement path is bound to an explicit recorded human decision over exact subject bytes. src/state/gates.ts:764-789 applies adopt-committed-deletions only after re-deriving the live newest-per-path projections and requiring each deleted path to still match its recorded digest and still be missing, otherwise failing closed with baseline-adoption-deletion-stale; the bytes arm at :740-762 does the same for observed digests. src/state/gate-decision-interface.ts:73 refuses a deletion decision when the context carries no deleted projections, so only context-satisfiable choices are offered, and the presentation carries an explicit labeled consequence (:216). The produce re-entry offer (src/state/next-action.ts:314-322) records no authority of its own — it reopens a write window whose bytes still pass the ordinary review and approval boundary — and once only committed deletions remain, routing hands over to the human gate (:323-332). Produce-time planned-final-phase re-derivation reads only bytes recorded in the produce subject, which remain subject to the phase's own review and approval gate, and it cannot shrink the bound below the producing phase (src/state/planned-final-phase.ts:130-137; src/mcp/handlers/state.ts:293-303).
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: New human decision arm adopt-committed-deletions in the baseline-adoption gate, migration-audit acceptance as the design-phase exit/commit authority, and the produce re-entry routing that replaces an unreachable inspect-state wedge.

rule_findings.rationale: Non-success states stay visible with a safe next action rather than being represented as success. Non-conforming or wedging produces fail closed with named issue codes produce-design-phase-plan-invalid and produce-derived-final-phase-below-current (src/mcp/handlers/state.ts:288-303), the latter explicitly directing the human toward a backward planning restart. Previously unreachable positions now yield a client-reachable action instead of a dead inspect-state (src/state/next-action.ts:294-332), and unresolvable cases still route to a human decision rather than silently adopting bytes. impl-notes.md reports the codex probe flake and its blocked_journey_hosts=1 run honestly alongside the clean rerun, states plainly that the design's self-cutover reinstalls were not performed, and records the interrupted-transaction atomicity gap and the re-entry guard's phase-kind blind spot as known limitations rather than claiming them fixed.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: Several failure/limitation states are reported in this change: the interrupted-produce wedge, the codex real-host probe flake, the skipped self-cutover installs, and two produce-settlement refusals.

rule_findings.rationale: Every new read identifies the exact task and subject bytes it governs. plannedFinalPhaseFromRecordedPayloads matches only `.archflow/tasks/${taskId}/design.md` from the transaction's own prepared payloads (src/state/planned-final-phase.ts:110-112), and loadApprovedDesignFinalPhase re-verifies artifact kind, phase, step, document path, manifest.artifact_digest against record.subject_digest and the payload digest before trusting bytes (:70-81). Adoption overlays require a bound prior recorded projection and fail closed with reconciliation-projection-unbound otherwise (src/state/reconciliation-discovery.ts:187-222), and the HEAD-absence probe distinguishes exit 128 from other failures rather than collapsing them (:281-289). The archivedBaselineAdoptionRequestV1Schema twin (src/contracts/durable-gate.ts:320) only relaxes the decisions tuple for pre-change archives; gate/task/subject bindings are still authenticated at resolution (src/state/gates.ts:740-789).
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: New durable authority reads: adoption-record overlays in projection discovery, the design-payload path used for planned-final-phase re-derivation, and the tolerant archived baseline-adoption request twin.
